papers.abstract: First-order phase transitions can source a stochastic gravitational-wave background within reach of LISA and other future detectors, with sound waves in the plasma typically providing the dominant contribution. Predicting the resulting gravitational-wave signal requires determining the stationary fluid profiles around expanding bubbles. We present a complete hydrodynamic classification of these profiles in the constant-sound-speed model, which generalizes the bag model by allowing the sound speeds in front of and behind the wall, $c_+$ and $c_-$, to differ. Solving the matching conditions at the wall and evolving the surrounding plasma, we recover the known direct and inverse detonations, deflagrations, and hybrids, and uncover mixed hybrids, a new class with rarefaction waves on both sides of the wall and oppositely directed fluid flows. For a sufficiently pronounced hierarchy $c_+>c_-$, multiple stationary profiles can correspond to the same wall velocity $\xi_w$ and asymptotic transition strength $\alpha_N$. This non-uniqueness arises because this parametrization discards thermodynamic information and is resolved once the underlying microphysics is specified. We compute the kinetic-energy budget and acoustic gravitational-wave spectra within the sound-shell model, finding that mixed hybrids introduce no additional spectral feature and can be mimicked by ordinary direct or inverse hybrids with substantially different fluid profiles. Finally, we release Hydr\'oDex, a public code implementing the complete classification, profile construction, energy-budget calculation, and gravitational-wave prediction.

papers.title: ReliaGuard: Reconstruction-Aware Watermarking for Source Attribution and Blind Edit Localization
papers.abstract: Generative image editing can reconstruct the background outside the requested edit, weakening spatial watermark evidence even when the source identifier remains recoverable. This creates an ambiguity for blind localization: a weak watermark response may indicate either an intended edit or background reconstruction. We propose ReliaGuard, a reconstruction-aware watermarking framework that addresses this ambiguity through reconstruction-stable evidence writing and coarse-to-fine blind reading. The writer aligns keyed feature responses in the protected image and its variational autoencoder reconstruction while preserving a frozen source-attribution channel. A quantization-aware projection bounds the distortion of the released eight-bit image. The reader combines keyed responses with image context to refine a base localization map, then integrates native-resolution detail with multiscale features to estimate the edit region. It is trained on paired observations before and after image processing and requires only the received image and key at inference. On 300 source images and 900 editing cases from three domains, ReliaGuard achieves intersection-over-union scores of 85.61% for complete editing outputs and 94.90% for locally spliced outputs at thresholds calibrated to a nominal 1% background false-positive rate on complete outputs. The former exceeds the strongest baseline by 45.02 percentage points, while decoded identifier-bit accuracy reaches 100% in both conditions. Across seven image-processing families, the corresponding localization scores remain 81.01% and 86.49%, with identifier-bit accuracies of 92.76% and 92.79%. These results show that reconstruction-aware writing and contextual reading can jointly support source attribution and edit localization under generative editing and subsequent image processing.

papers.title: The importance of shear strain in narrow Si/SiGe quantum wells
papers.abstract: Several heterostructure profiles have been proposed for Si/SiGe quantum wells, to improve the operation of quantum-dot spin qubits. These structures share a common goal of generating either of the two wave vectors that govern the conduction-band valley coupling, dubbed $k_0$ and $k_1$. Here, we focus on the long-wavelength $k_1$ term that couples valleys when paired with shear strain, and which governs the Dresselhaus spin-orbit coupling. We show that shear strain induced by metal top gates may be enough to activate the $k_1$ valley-coupling mechanism, mitigating the need for "ultrasharp" interfaces, as commonly assumed for large valley energy splittings. We propose a scheme featuring narrow quantum wells that does not require ultrasharp interfaces, but should still provide large deterministic valley splittings (when paired with shear strain), and large spin-orbit couplings and $g$-factor corrections, which are of great interest for experimental implementations.

papers.title: $L^p$ Integrability and Spectral Complexity of Manifolds with Higher Codimension
papers.abstract: We investigate the relationship between the $L^p$ integrability of functions and the curvature geometry of their Fourier support. We prove that if $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a $C^n$ manifold of dimension $d$ and $n>2d$, then every $u\in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\widehat u\subseteq M$ vanishes whenever \[ 2\le p\le\frac{6n-4}{3d-1}. \] This strictly improves the classical threshold $2n/d$ throughout the range $n>2d$. More generally, we obtain a family of dimension-dependent improvements in higher codimension. As a consequence, we obtain a strict quantitative improvement in the necessary conditions for Fourier restriction when $n>2d$, resolving a conjecture of Mockenhaupt \cite{Mockenhaupt96}. This further establishes the nonexistence of quadratic manifolds satisfying the Christ--Mockenhaupt condition when $n>2d$, answering the question of \cite{CLMP}. For quadratic manifolds, we obtain spectral synthesis bounds from joint sublevel estimates for the eigenvalues of the normal Hessian pencil. In codimension two, we determine the exact critical exponent from the ranks and eigenvalue vanishing orders, including nonexistence at the critical endpoint. We also obtain integrability bounds for manifolds with constant relative nullity, extending Guo's hypersurface results \cite{Guo93} to higher codimension. Finally, we use the Fourier ratio as a measure of the geometric complexity of individual strata of the characteristic set to establish $L^p$ uniqueness criteria for homogeneous constant-coefficient PDEs.

papers.title: DuoJEPA: Cross-Modal Translation Between Unaligned Self-Supervised Embedding Spaces
papers.abstract: Learning from paired modalities is commonly equated with aligning them: two encoders are trained until the embeddings of a pair coincide in a shared space. We study whether cross-modal retrieval and classification can instead be obtained while the two encoders' own embedding spaces remain directly unaligned. DuoJEPA trains one encoder per modality with the self-supervised LeJEPA objective and appends to each encoder a single transformer layer that translates its embedding into the other encoder's space, supervised by a contrastive objective computed entirely within that target space. No loss term compares the two own spaces directly, although the encoders are optimised jointly through the translation objective. In our experiments, the translator's residual connections determine where the cross-modal pressure is absorbed: with a residual translator the two encoders become directly aligned, whereas with a skipless (residual-free) translator a paired-cosine test detects no alignment in the final models, and at most a weak one in the ablations, at comparable cross-modal performance. The learned class-token translation is well approximated by a single scaled rotation of the source space. We evaluate DuoJEPA on two modality pairs that differ in nearly every respect. On chest radiographs and reports from CheXpert Plus, it attains a zero-shot AUC of 86.6 and a cross-modal retrieval score of 78.5, compared with 60.0 and 64.2 for our reimplementation of LeVLJEPA with the same encoders and data. On Sentinel-2 optical and Sentinel-1 radar imagery, the frozen encoders fall within the range of published Sentinel foundation models under our reproduction of the Copernicus-Bench linear-probe protocol, the translator retrieves the paired image of the other sensor among 4,000 candidates in 77-79% of cases, and a patch-level extension transfers the within-image similarity structure of the scene.

papers.title: Where Is Uncertainty Observed? A Mechanistic Understanding of Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs
papers.abstract: Knowing when a large language model's (LLM's) response can be trusted is critical for its safe use. Uncertainty quantification (UQ) can help LLMs recognize if their responses may be unreliable. Existing taxonomies organize UQ methods by uncertainty source or estimation mechanism. They leave unresolved the question of where uncertainty is observed in the model's computation. The answer matters because the observation point determines whether an estimator has access to enough information to recover a given target, and how well it can recover it. Drawing on mechanistic interpretability, we define four mechanistic observation lenses: the structural lens observes component updates, the representational lens observes hidden states, the distributional lens observes token probabilities, and the semantical lens observes distributions over meanings. We relate these lenses through the residual stream and order them by the information they carry, which gives a principle for selecting UQ methods for different targets. We survey existing methods through the four lenses. Furthermore, we distinguish evaluation targets, criteria, and metrics to clarify different UQ evaluation protocols. Finally, we identify open problems and research directions to connect uncertainty estimation to the internal computation and downstream use of LLMs.

papers.title: $^{55}$Mn-NMR/NQR study on the kagome metal Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$: Re-examining the possibility of spin-singlet paired state
papers.abstract: Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$ is a Mn-based kagome metal that has been proposed to be close to a ferromagnetic instability. Recent $^{55}$Mn nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) study suggested the emergence of a spin-singlet paired state below $\sim$10 K. To clarify its low-energy magnetic and electronic properties, we performed $^{55}$Mn NMR and nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR) measurements on single-crystalline Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$. From the detailed NMR/NQR spectrum measurements and the DFT calculations, a quadrupolar frequency of $\nu_{\rm Q}$ = 4.6$\sim$4.8 MHz and an asymmetry parameter of $\eta$ = 0.45$\sim$0.48 as well as the principal axes of electric field gradient EFG for the Mn site were determined. The temperature dependence of Knight shift ($K$) shows a similar temperature dependence of the DC magnetic susceptibility $\chi$ except for the low-temperature region below $\sim$ 50 K where $K$ is almost constant while $\chi$ keeps increasing, which suggests that the increase in $\chi$ at low temperatures is not intrinsic. $^{55}$Mn spin-lattice relaxation rate divided by temperature ($1/T_1T$) is found to be nearly constant, confirming the metallic state of Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$ from a microscopic point of view. Furthermore, no peak in $1/T_1T$ is observed near 10 K, and neither the Knight shift nor the linewidth shows any reductions at low temperatures. These results suggest no clear signature for the spin-singlet pairing around 10 K in Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$.

papers.title: Experimental Evidence for MeV Undulator Radiation Generated by Ultrarelativistic Positrons in a Periodically Bent Crystal
papers.abstract: We report evidence for undulator radiation generated by ultrarelativistic positrons in a large-amplitude, long-period crystalline undulator. A pattern of Si$_3$N$_4$ stressors periodically bend the (110) planes of a Silicon crystal with a geometry measured independently by x-ray diffraction. Under planar alignment, the forward energy loss showed a localized excess at $6.8 \pm 0.3$~MeV, matching the predictions of simulations. Experimental results also indicate that an intense positron beam could make the undulator competitive in brilliance with state-of-the-art inverse-Compton gamma-ray sources.

papers.title: Whether untrained networks beat trained ones at V1 depends on a normalisation convention: evidence from two fMRI datasets
papers.abstract: Untrained convolutional networks have been reported to rival or beat trained networks as models of primary visual cortex (V1), and we had reported such an advantage in THINGS fMRI. Under a pre-specified ridge readout, the trained network was ahead at every pooling grid in THINGS and in NSD (8 of 8 subjects), also when voxel responses were centred within runs. Representational similarity analysis (RSA) in THINGS depended on analysis choices (28 analyses: intervals above 0 in 5, below 0 in 9, including 0 in 14); in NSD with its standard normalisation, none of 28 analyses favoured the untrained network. The untrained advantage appears when a response profile common to all trials is left in the voxel patterns and model units are not centred, under correlation distance: removing the session-mean profile in THINGS reduced it from +0.030 to +0.005; with raw betas it reached +0.100 in THINGS, appeared in the THINGS test images, and appeared in NSD (+0.116, 8 of 8 subjects, a pre-specified prediction), where it was confined to this one of 28 analyses. With the profile left in, both representational dissimilarity matrices are dominated by per-image response amplitude, which in V1 tracks contrast energy, and the untrained network's matrix is more amplitude-dominated; the amplitude itself is matched equally by both networks; removing the amplitude structure from both matrices removes the advantage in NSD (+0.116 to -0.009, 8 of 8 subjects). A luminance-and-contrast baseline outperformed every network under ridge in both datasets (point estimates); the networks reached 10-15% of the NSD noise-ceiling lower bound. 24 of 88 pre-specified predictions were not met. We recommend centring or normalising voxel responses within session, reporting the sensitivity of RSA rankings to this choice and to model-unit centring, and replicating on a second dataset.

papers.title: Multi-pump amplification of frequency-separated Stokes waves in stimulated Brillouin side scattering
papers.abstract: Multibeam stimulated Brillouin side scattering (SBSS) can be enhanced when one side-scattered light wave is amplified by several pump waves through different ion-acoustic waves (IAWs). This mechanism differs from models in which several pumps share the same scattered-light wave or the same IAW. Side-scattered light generated by different pumps can propagate in nearly the same direction but have different frequencies. We examine this process using a local temporal-growth calculation, a finite-width Gaussian k-space model, a three-dimensional envelope model, and two-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. These cross-beam three-wave interactions increase temporal growth and convective gain over the crossing angles considered. In the three-dimensional envelope calculations, direct SBS interactions alone produce weak, localized side scattering, whereas including the cross-beam interactions produces a strong response for the same incident fields and initial perturbations. The enhancement remains when the total incident power is fixed, so it comes from the cross-beam interactions rather than from extra laser power. The PIC simulations show stronger side scattering and several pump-specific IAWs, with a non-monotonic dependence on beam number. These results identify cross-beam amplification of frequency-separated side-scattered light as a gain pathway that should be considered when interpreting multibeam SBS experiments.

papers.title: $\varepsilon$-WM: Error-Driven Dynamics Adaptation across Fast--Slow Timescales for World Modeling
papers.abstract: A core challenge for world models is adapting to sudden, persistent, yet initially unknown changes in robot dynamics. If the world model fails to adapt, its prediction errors accumulate over the open-loop rollout and ultimately mislead the robot's actions. Existing world models, however, struggle to balance three key requirements for dynamics adaptation: responsiveness, rapidly correcting sudden changes; stability, avoiding lasting model updates from transient disturbances; and persistence, retaining adapted dynamics during the observation-free open-loop rollout. Inspired by multi-timescale predictive coding in the human brain, we propose $\varepsilon$-WM, a world model that adapts to unknown dynamics through error-driven corrections across fast and slow timescales. $\varepsilon$-WM incorporates three novel features: 1) Multiple internal experts (MiE) emulate neural pathway reweighting, each combining a fixed base expert with fast--slow adaptation networks. 2) Fast--slow timescale adaptation captures distinct adaptation dynamics: fast states respond rapidly and decay, whereas slow states accumulate corrections and persist. 3) Predictive correction uses prediction errors to update fast and slow states and reweight experts without gradients. During open-loop rollout, each expert feeds back its own predictions, and $\varepsilon$-WM aggregates their outputs through adaptive weighting. Extensive experiments show $\varepsilon$-WM has a consistently lower multi-step mean error than all ten baselines on six datasets, verifying the effectiveness of each feature.

papers.title: Kitaev Exchange and Altermagnetism in the Double Perovskite Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$: An Ab Initio Study
papers.abstract: The Co$^{2+}$-based double perovskite Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ attracts attention due to its nontrivial magnetic properties. \textit{Ab initio} density functional theory calculations reveal a substantial ferromagnetic Kitaev exchange $|K|\sim J/3$ between nearest neighbors that, combined with the face-centered cubic lattice, leads to pronounced exchange frustration and places Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ among Kitaev materials with moderate Kitaev interaction strength. In addition, Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ is found to be altermagnetic with a sizable non-relativistic spin splitting, which can give rise to a transverse piezomagnetic effect and a nontrivial magneto-optical response.

papers.title: A Cardiorespiratory Foundation Model Pretrained on Ten Physiological Signals for Perioperative and Critical Care
papers.abstract: Arterial, venous, pulmonary artery, and intracranial pressures and ventilator waveforms guide decisions in operating rooms and intensive care units, yet foundation models for physiological waveforms rely almost entirely on the electrocardiogram and photoplethysmogram. We present the CArdio-Respiratory Multi-modal ENcoder (CARMEN), a single encoder pretrained without labels on ten cardiorespiratory waveforms (2.27 million modality-hours). CARMEN accepts any combination of co-recorded signals at variable lengths. A conditioning mechanism, LSCNorm, restores the absolute signal level removed by normalization; in a matched ablation, replacing it with standard normalization lowered the AUROC for intraoperative hypotension by 0.11. Across 19 tasks from Korean and US cohorts, the frozen encoder significantly outperformed both supervised models in 12 of the 15 tasks on which they were evaluated. It outperformed three pretrained foundation models on 14--17 of 19 tasks, and none of them exceeded it on any task. Given the electrocardiogram or photoplethysmogram alone, it matched or exceeded the signal-specific foundation models in most comparisons, and the performance was largely preserved even after removing the secondary channels.

papers.title: RSI-PDEbench: A Benchmark for Self-Improving Agents in PDE Solving
papers.abstract: Identifying and solving partial differential equations (PDEs) from sampled solution data often requires substantial expert effort in equation discovery, coefficient estimation, and numerical solver configuration, especially under noise and distribution shifts. Can large language model (LLM) agents automate this workflow accurately and efficiently? To investigate this question, we introduce RSI-PDEbench, a benchmark of 1,001 cases spanning 42 equation templates, including both classical and fractional PDEs. It provides three evaluation settings: Full evaluates performance on noise-free solution data; Noisy tests robustness to Gaussian noise with an RMS equal to 50\% of the clean-signal RMS; and Hard-OOD tests challenging out-of-distribution generalization to unseen equation templates and shifted coefficient ranges. We further introduce RSI-PDE, a recursively self-improving agent harness that shortlists candidate equations by residual loss, uses relative $L^2$ feedback to refine coefficients and numerical solvers, and applies a validation gate to policy and memory updates. We compare RSI-PDE with single-run baselines and native agent harnesses (Claude Code or Codex) across four frontier models. Across the three settings, RSI-PDE improves the pass rate averaged across the four models by 106.5--181.9\% relative to single-run baselines and by 3.0--19.6\% relative to native harnesses, while reducing total recorded model calls by 46.9\% across the 12 model--setting pairs. These results highlight the potential of validated recursive self-improvement in LLM agents to advance scientific computing.

papers.title: A nonfinitely based additively idempotent semiring with finitely based matrix semirings
papers.abstract: We establish that the matrix semiring $\mathbf{M}_n(SR_6)$ over the six-element nonfinitely based additively idempotent semiring $SR_6$ is finitely based for every $n \geq 2$. This provides the first known example of an additively idempotent semiring $S$ that is nonfinitely based, while the matrix semirings $\mathbf{M}_n(S)$ are finitely based. Moreover, we show that the interval $[\mathsf{V}(SR_6), \mathsf{V}(\mathbf{M}_2(SR_6))]$ in the lattice of additively idempotent semiring varieties has the cardinality of the continuum.

papers.title: $G_2'$-Slodowy Slices II: Anosov Representations
papers.abstract: We find many exotic connected components of Anosov representations of surface groups in the split real group $G_2'$ that are neither $\iota$-Fuchsian deformations nor higher rank Teichm\"uller spaces. These representations are found through the non-abelian Hodge correspondence via $G_2'$-Higgs bundles that we call $\alpha$-bundles and $\beta$-bundles, which are particular cyclic Higgs bundles in the Slodowy slices of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triples associated to the simple roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of $\mathfrak{g}_2^{\mathbb{C}}$. We first prove that (most) $\beta$-bundles that are also Hodge bundles are $P_{\beta}$-Anosov and $\alpha$-bundles are $P_{\alpha}$-Anosov. The strategy employed is new, geometric, and general. For $\sigma \in \{\alpha, \beta\}$, we then show the locally homogeneous $(G_2', G_2'/P_{\sigma})$-manifold $\mathscr{M}_{\sigma}(\rho)$ recently described in arXiv:2510.12757, for the representation $\rho:\pi_1S\rightarrow \mathsf{G}_2'$ associated to a $\sigma$-bundle, coincides up to finite cover with the corresponding geometric structure for $\rho$ defined via domains of discontinuity by Guichard-Wienhard and Kapovich-Leeb-Porti. Consequently, we find that $\pi_1({\mathscr{M}}_{\sigma}(\rho))$ is an invariant for the connected component of $\rho$ in the space of $P_{\sigma}$-Anosov representations. After verifying the folklore result that the $G_2'$-character variety has exactly three connected components, we conclude lower bounds for the number of connected components of $P_{\sigma}$-Anosov representations in the two non-Hitchin components, most of which are exotic. These are the first higher rank examples of connected components of a character variety containing multiple (in fact, arbitrarily many) exotic components of Anosov representations.

papers.title: Mutual Linearity in Nonlinear Population Dynamics
papers.abstract: Mutual linearity, the persistence of affine relations among stationary observables under arbitrarily strong changes of one transition rate, is known for Markov jump processes and chemical reaction networks. We show that generalized Lotka--Volterra dynamics form a new class of mutually linear systems, even though species can go extinct and attractors can be chaotic. Any change to one species' equation acts on the others as one effective press and keeps all abundances affinely related: piecewise across extinctions, and as time averages on chaotic attractors.

papers.title: Linking Outer Solar System Objects in Archival DECam Imaging: A Multi-year Linker Tested on Held-out Known Objects, and 273 Multi-opposition Candidates Including Six L4 Neptune Trojans, Two Retrograde Objects and Ten with a > 150 au
papers.abstract: I link single-night detections in public DECam imaging: 74% of the NOIRLab Source Catalog DR2 (2012-2019) sky with four or more nights, and my extraction from 149,421 exposures (2020-2026). Of 931 secure known objects, single-season linking recovers 22.1-25.0%, a multi-year linker 26.5%, together 36.2%. The multi-year rule, fixed before its held-out tests, recovers 68% of DES objects brighter than r=23.5 in a strip of its footprint and 14 of 47 known objects outside it. Its shifted-sky controls, complete for 162 of 165 blocks, return no candidate. This limits pure chance alignments, not links that mix real and chance detections. An identity check by orbit with 3,110 joint fits finds no designated object among the candidates. Searches beyond 79 au recover, blind, only 2014 UZ224, Gonggong and Chiminigagua. The catalogue has 273 undesignated candidates with orbits from two or more oppositions, whose linked detections were re-measured on the images; of the 189 of version 2, 41 were then detected on two or more nights that their fits did not use. Listed apart are 92 weaker entries and 30 designated objects, 17 of them Rubin discoveries with 2.9-13.2 yr of arc before discovery. Six are candidate L4 Neptune Trojans whose orbits and clones librate for 10 Myr (one reported independently by Jongma 2026, mostly from other data), two are retrograde candidates and ten have a>150 au. There is no follow-up or validated selection function. The Minor Planet Center has astrometry of 38 objects; unreleased positions are available on request, in confidence.

papers.title: Virtual Two-Step Nilpotency of the Fundamental Groups of Special Quasi-Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that the fundamental group of every smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety that is special in the sense of Campana is virtually nilpotent of class at most two. This establishes the two-step nilpotency conjecture of Cao--Deng--Hacon--P\u{a}un, a quasi-projective analogue of Campana's almost abelian conjecture for special compact K\"ahler manifolds. Examples of Cadorel--Deng--Yamanoi show that the step bound is sharp. On a suitable finite etale cover, we construct a canonical second Albanese map to a torus torsor over an abelian variety. The proof reduces to showing that the kernel of the induced map on fundamental groups is finite. Using good minimal models and meridian groups of projective pairs, we show that an infinite kernel would yield a saturated rank-one subsheaf of logarithmic differentials whose Iitaka dimension contradicts specialness.

papers.title: Emilia2: A Large-Scale Dataset for Controllable Long-Form Speech Generation
papers.abstract: Generating long-form speech requires models to keep content, speaker identity, turn-taking, and expressive style consistent over time. Yet most open training corpora contain examples lasting only tens of seconds and open long-form benchmarks cover at most two speakers per recording. We introduce Emilia2, a 229K-hour multilingual dataset for controllable long-form speech generation. From in-the-wild data, Emilia2 constructs short utterances, single-speaker long-form speech, and multi-speaker dialogues, preserving transcripts, speaker identities, pauses, and acoustic transitions. Examples longer than five minutes account for 50.0% of single-speaker long-form hours and 66.8% of dialogue hours. To support expressive control, Emilia2 provides natural language instructions for 4.77M examples and nonverbal-vocalization tags for 933K examples. We also introduce Emilia2-testset, 23 hours of bilingual recordings of up to 30 minutes and four speakers, each speaker paired with reference audio. We train autoregressive (AR) and non-autoregressive (NAR) models on Emilia2. Our 0.6B-backbone NAR model achieves the lowest Chinese CER and English WER on TTSD-Eval (5.27%/9.93%) among compared systems, while our AR model is on par with Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-VD on InstructTTSEval (zh/en: 76.2/78.3 vs. 77.1/77.9). These results validate Emilia2 as a comprehensive data foundation for long-form speech generation and minute-scale expressive control. Demo: https://charlesnii.github.io/Emilia2-demo/.

papers.title: The WoW: A Large-Scale World Knowledge Corpus for Full-Lifecycle LLM Training
papers.abstract: Existing Chinese educational corpora often suffer from fragmented coverage and a lack of systematic organization. In this paper, we propose WoW (\textbf{Wo}rld Kno\textbf{w}ledge), a large-scale dataset designed for the full-cycle training of foundation models. The construction of this dataset is driven by an Educational Knowledge Graph, which serves as a taxonomic backbone for the systematic collection and completion of missing educational modules across all levels. Compared to previous versions, this iteration provides enhanced systematicity, superior quality, and a larger scale, while incorporating multimodal signals and supporting every stage of model development. Experiments demonstrate that WoW significantly improves model performance across diverse benchmarks. To facilitate community research, we further provide an interactive platform for graph-based data selection and retrieval.
authors: Yuanjian Xu (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)

papers.title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
papers.abstract: Scalar-induced second-order tensor perturbations comprise both a forced response and freely propagating gravitational waves, the radiative signal sought in observations. We define this free radiation as the out-state, whose amplitudes are given by the light-cone residue of the kernel for each scalar pair via a classical LSZ-type reduction formula. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: tensor redefinitions whose shifts have power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leave the out-state invariant. For any constant equation of state $0<w<1$, the out-state is consequently universal across all intrinsic gauges, in which the slicing and spatial coordinates are fixed locally by matter and geometry without an external clock. This class includes the comoving and uniform-density gauges, whose spectra grow without bound at late times in radiation domination. Over this range of $w$, the late-time Newtonian-gauge kernel yields the out-state, justifying its standard use in computing the gravitational-wave energy spectrum. In matter domination, by contrast, the out-state isolates the free wave from the static tidal response that asymptotically dominates the Newtonian-gauge tensor perturbation.

papers.title: Extending indoor airborne infection risk modelling to 3D, with local surface deposition
papers.abstract: Mathematical models of indoor disease transmission often rely on simplifying assumptions to reduce computational cost. In particular, in the Viral Infection Risk Indoor Simulator (VIRIS)[13], which combines architectural layout, people movement and airborne viral transmission, aerosol concentrations are assumed uniform across room height, allowing a two-dimensional (2D) formulation. Also, particle deposition on surfaces is represented by a first-order removal term acting throughout the computational domain. Here, we extend VIRIS to the VIRIS-3D-L framework to investigate how these two assumptions affect the predicted infection risk. In VIRIS-3D-L, we solve the reaction-diffusion equation in three dimensions (3D), and aerosol deposition is represented by local surface removal through a Robin boundary condition. We compare VIRIS with VIRIS-3D-L across three indoor settings of increasing architectural and people-movement complexity: a courtroom, a care home, and a supermarket. For the courtroom, care home, and supermarket, respectively, at the end of the simulation, the original 2D formulation with global removal predicts average infection risks across individuals of 44%, 78%, and 25%, while VIRIS-3D-L predicts risks of 51%, 85%, and 28%. Thus, VIRIS significantly underestimates infection risk in all three settings. The predictions of VIRIS-3D-L also show agreement with a documented courtroom outbreak that was used to validate VIRIS. Although computation time increases by approximately a factor of four on average, simulations remain feasible on a standard laptop, taking between eight minutes and just under 1.5 hours. These findings suggest that VIRIS-3D-L offers a more physically realistic framework for assessing indoor airborne infection risk in indoor spaces without prohibitive computational costs.

papers.title: Stabilization of zero forcing numbers of finite quotients of periodic graphs
papers.abstract: We give a method for determining the zero forcing number of a graph by passing to an infinite cover. When the quotient map is a covering map, forcing commutes with taking preimages. If, in addition, the closure of every small set in the cover touches none of its translates, then no small set is a zero forcing set of the quotient. For covers that are periodic, this condition reduces to a property of the cover alone, and it gives an explicit threshold beyond which the zero forcing number of the quotient equals that of the cover. We apply the method to the generalized Petersen graphs: $Z(P(n,k))=2k+2$ for all $k\ge 1$ and $n\ge 2k^2+k+1$. We also show that the circulant $C_n(1,a)$ has zero forcing number $2a$ for all $n\ge 2a^2-a+1$.

papers.title: Brown Measures and Spectral Convergence for Arbitrary GUE Polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every noncommutative polynomial in independent GUE matrices, the empirical eigenvalue distribution converges almost surely to the Brown measure of the same polynomial in free semicircular variables. This is the Gaussian case of a conjecture of Belinschi, \'Sniady and Speicher. We also prove that the spectrum converges almost surely in Hausdorff distance to the spectrum of the limiting operator, so that the spectral radius converges as well; deviations have probability smaller than every inverse power of the matrix size. For this we show that the support of the Brown measure of every polynomial in free semicircular variables is its whole spectrum, a statement about operators that involves no random matrices. We also give an algorithm, with a convergence guarantee, that computes the limiting Brown measure from matrices whose size depends only on the polynomial. A holomorphic rotation introduces an independent Ginibre component and yields the almost-sure limit without a least-singular-value bound for the original GUE polynomial. We also give a second-moment criterion for weak convergence of Brown measures. On free probability side, we use the Dyson equation of a linear pencil to show that harmonicity of its logarithmic potential forces invertibility.

papers.title: Concave shifts and the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a non-zero reproducing kernel Hilbert space of holomorphic functions on the unit disc, and assume $\mathcal{H}$ is invariant under the forward and backward shifts. We show that if the forward shift on $\mathcal{H}$ is concave, then $\mathcal{H}$ is a complete Nevanlinna--Pick (CNP) space. This answers a question by Shimorin, and greatly extends his result that any space of Dirichlet type is CNP. As a byproduct of our investigation, we also show that if the forward shift on $\mathcal{H}$ is concave, then any multiplier of $\mathcal{H}$ is the SOT limit of its Ces\`aro means. As applications, we prove a commutant lifting theorem for concave cyclic analytic operators, and several results about shift-invariant subspaces in de~Branges--Rovnyak spaces.

papers.title: Computing EF1 Allocations under Budget Constraints in Polynomial Time
papers.abstract: We study the allocation of indivisible goods to agents with budgets and additive valuations. Each agent compares its bundle with every budget-feasible subset of another agent's bundle or of the unallocated goods. We give a strongly polynomial algorithm for computing an allocation that is envy-free up to one good (EF1), even when agents have different valuations and budgets. Deciding whether a given allocation satisfies EF1 is coNP-complete. Equivalently, deciding whether it violates EF1 is NP-complete. When all agents have the same valuation, we can compute an EF1 allocation with welfare at least $(1/2-\varepsilon)$ times the maximum feasible welfare in time polynomial in the input length and $1/\varepsilon$, for any $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. Finding an allocation that is envy-free up to any good (EFX) is NP-hard even for one agent. We give polynomial-time EFX algorithms when each agent values goods in proportion to their sizes or when the number of distinct positive item values per agent is bounded by a constant.

papers.title: Direct Conditioning of Audio Diffusion Transformers on fMRI Reveals Cortical Contributions to Sound Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Reconstructing audio from brain activity remains challenging. Existing brain-to-audio pipelines typically map neural responses to predefined stimulus representations before synthesis. While recent work in the visual domain has explored direct conditioning on brain activity, this approach has not yet been extended to audio diffusion models. We introduce MAAS (Multi-Area Auditory Synthesis), an end-to-end framework that conditions a pretrained audio diffusion transformer on ROI-wise fMRI responses without first supervising a decoder to predict an external stimulus representation. MAAS uses region-specific projections and learned brain tokens to condition Stable Audio through a dedicated cross-attention pathway. On a 7T fMRI dataset, we demonstrate consistent improvements over baselines, including two-stage fMRI-to-latent conditioning, across both acoustic and semantic evaluation metrics. In addition, we introduce a fidelity metric grounded in a computational model of auditory neural processing, which allows us to quantify the contribution of individual auditory cortical regions to reconstructed audio representations.

papers.title: Out-of-the-Box Tabular Foundation Models for Bayesian Optimization in Materials Discovery
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization is widely used in active learning loops for materials science. Gaussian processes serve as the de-facto surrogate model family, but require task-dependent kernel choices and can lack the modeling capacity for complex relationships. Tabular foundation models (TFMs) have recently emerged as the state-of-the-art for predictive tasks on structured data, without requiring bespoke kernels or hyperparameter tuning. We evaluate two TFMs, TabPFN and TabICL, as out-of-the-box surrogate models on two standard materials science benchmarks, comparing against a large field of baselines encompassing Gaussian processes, random forests, and CatBoost. Our findings indicate that TFMs are highly competitive surrogate models across the two benchmarks, without task-specific training for active learning or GP kernel selection. Our results motivate developing TFMs further as surrogates for active learning in materials discovery.

papers.title: Measuring Generative AI Content in Political Campaigns: Evidence of Rising Adoption and Non-Disclosure
papers.abstract: The use of generative AI in political campaigns has drawn public concern and policy attention. Public concerns range from distrust of candidates to skepticism about the authenticity and accuracy of political advertising, including AI-generated images and video. Nearly half of U.S. states have enacted laws that prohibit, or require disclosure of, "materially deceptive" AI-generated content (AIGC) in elections to guard against these concerns. This study measures how candidates and their campaigns produce and circulate AIGC during an election cycle. We develop two measures that estimate not only wether campaigns use AIGC, but how much they produce (magnitude) and in what forms (modality). We apply these measures to a novel dataset of text and images from the campaign websites, X accounts, and emails of 12,977 candidates for U.S. political office from 2023 to 2025. We report three findings. First, detectable AIGC from campaigns increased significantly across modalities over the observation window, and campaigns that use AIGC frequently do not disclose it. Second, incumbents' campaigns produced significantly less AIGC than challengers' campaigns. Third, candidates in states with AIGC disclosure or prohibition laws do not produce measurably less AIGC than candidates in other states. Our method and findings have implications for transparency and trust in elections, and on state laws that regulate AI use in campaigns. Because current state laws largely target mainly "materially deceptive" content, we identify additional policy mechanisms that could increase electoral transparency and improve trust as AIGC becomes more prevalent.

papers.title: Karhunen-Lo\`eve Transforms of Autoregressive Windows Based on Matched Symmetry Groups
papers.abstract: The Karhunen-Lo\`eve transform of a window of a stationary autoregressive process of any order $p$ is described through its poles, extending the Algebraic Diversity framework, which selects a transform by the matched group. For simple roots every basis vector is a sum of at most $p$ sinusoids, at the frequencies where the spectrum equals the eigenvalue, plus modes decaying from the ends. The window covariance differs from a member of the class diagonalized by the type-II discrete cosine transform by a closed-form matrix of rank $2p$, exactly when no pole is zero, so the eigenvalues interlace spectrum samples on the cosine grid, and the coding-gain loss of the cosine transform is an exact function of that matrix, below 1.2 percent for the $8\times8$ Markov block at pole $0.95$. By Kronecker's theorem the rank is at most $2\max(p,q)$ for rational spectra. A moving-average window departs in its Hankel corners, and an integrated (ARIMA) window departs by low rank from the type-VII sine class, exactly for the random walk. The exact symmetry is generically the reflection and contains a wreath product for interleaved windows. The dihedral group of the even extension is matched approximately, the dominant pole's sign choosing cosine or sine. The two groups give the transform a fast form: a parity fold, half-length cosine cores and a cascade of at most $p$ first-order Cauchy stages, exactly $p$ for a minimal AR($p$) model. The first-order case recovers results obtained by other means. This version adds complex data on the cyclic group with a border departure of rank exactly $2p$, the mixed and integrated classes, odd-length cores, and a released implementation whose kernel evaluation counts are flat in $M\log_2(M/n_{\mathrm{leaf}})$ to 5.3 percent. Experiments on recorded acoustic-array, radar and vibration data state where the transform helps and where existing methods match it.

papers.title: Ostinato: Low-Latency CPU-GPU MoE Inference for Local Agents
papers.abstract: Language-model agents increasingly run on local workstations with consumer GPUs, where quantized mixture-of-experts (MoE) models split routed experts between GPU and host memory. Prefix-cached agent sessions alternate single-token decode with short tool-return prefills, typically up to a few hundred tokens. Short tool turns touch more experts than consumer GPUs can hold, yet direct roughly 85% of DeepSeek-V4-Flash's routes to a static GPU pool while leaving 3.3-5.5 tokens per cold expert. Widely used local engines such as llama.cpp and KTransformers either copy tens of gigabytes over PCIe per turn, compute every route on the CPU while idling resident GPU experts, or budget GPU memory by whole layers and uniform per-layer quotas. We present Ostinato, a CPU-GPU MoE engine that reuses one static cross-layer GPU pool in place across every forward pass. During decode and short tool turns, Ostinato computes resident routes on the GPUs and sparse cold routes on the CPU, so short turns copy no expert weights; on long prefills, it deduplicates cold uploads; and for multi-GPU decode, all-zero expert slots with device-side synchronization capture each GPU's decode step in one CUDA graph. Across held-out SWE and -bench sessions on three MoE models, Ostinato cuts median tool-turn waits by 2.5-6.6x and finishes sessions 1.36-3.83x faster than default baselines, staying 1.30-1.94x faster when baselines align their upload threshold and weight loading. It finishes sessions fastest across seven agent workloads, one to four GPUs, and up to eight concurrent sessions, while its cross-layer pool speeds up 335 GB DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash by 1.81-2.19x over llama.cpp's expert cache.

papers.title: On the connected zero forcing polynomial of finite trees
papers.abstract: Given a graph $\Gamma$ with vertex set $V(\Gamma)$ and a set of colored vertices S, the zero forcing rule is an iterative graph coloring process which states that a colored vertex with exactly one uncolored neighbor forces that neighbor to become colored. If repeated application of this rule eventually colors every vertex of $\Gamma$, the set $S$ is called a \emph{zero forcing set}. Now, if the induced subgraph $\Gamma\vert_S$ is connected, then $S$ is called a \textit{connected zero forcing set}. The minimum cardinality of such a set is the \emph{connected zero forcing number} $Z_C(\Gamma)$. A \emph{connected zero forcing polynomial} of a finite graph $\Gamma$ is a monic polynomial $Z_C^{\Gamma}(x) \;=\; \sum_{k} a_k x^k$, where $a_k$ counts the number of connected zero forcing sets of $\Gamma$ of size $k$, which we denote by $Z_C(\Gamma,k)$. In this paper, we find the connected zero forcing polynomial of any finite tree $T$, and show that they are log-concave. We then establish sharp lower bounds for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices. We also identify a family of trees, which we call uniform trees, and we prove that for any tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, there exists a uniform tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, whose connected zero forcing polynomial bounds as an upper bound, the connected zero forcing polynomial of the tree coefficient wise. Again for $2\leq p\leq 4$, we establish a sharp upper bound for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices.

papers.title: Controlled Riemannian rigidity
papers.abstract: Given a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on a compact connected manifold, we prove that the space of invariant Riemannian metrics whose symmetry group is precisely the group in question is open dense in that of all invariant metrics provided the orbit space is at least 2-dimensional. This strengthens the author's prior results to their optimal dimension bound and recovers Ebin's non-equivariant analogue to the effect that trivial-symmetry Riemannian metrics constitute an open dense set. In the process, the discussion also addresses a number of apparent gaps in said sources, pertaining to the rigidity results in question.

papers.title: Smooth local isometric embeddings in dimension four
papers.abstract: Every smooth four-dimensional Riemannian metric admits a local isometric embedding into $\mathbb{R}^{10}$, the optimal universal dimension. A fixed-domain Nash-Moser argument prescribes any Gauss-compatible rank-six second fundamental form with regular characteristic data. For $n\ge4$, product-weighted cube evaluations give polynomial Gram lifts of algebraic curvature tensors that are uniformly positive on a fixed $n(n-1)/2$-dimensional support. In dimension four the support can have a nonsingular complex characteristic quartic. With linear tangential control, the transverse square-root estimate near affine embeddings is sharp in $H^\ell$ for $\ell\ge1$.

papers.title: Optimizing one-dimensional lithographically defined nanowires in semiconducting heterostructures
papers.abstract: One-dimensional nanowires can host remarkable electronic properties and are central to studying quantum transport. Although heterostructure-defined confinement combined with gate-defined potentials can greatly reduce the effects of impurities as measured via electron mobilities, the realization and interpretation of novel effects at this scale are complicated by disorder. Experiments on lithographically defined one-dimensional nanowires therefore do not exhibit ideal behavior. Using theoretical and computational models, we predict that optimizing the geometry of split gates in semiconducting heterostructures will lead to higher-quality channels for transport measurements. Further, we show that this optimization is essential for resolving features of interest such as the Rashba-induced spin gap. This new approach to lithographically defined conduction channels provides better energy resolution and is less susceptible to disorder.

papers.title: Polyhedral Geometry of Degree-Bounded Characteristic Imset Polytopes
papers.abstract: Characteristic imset polytopes are convex hulls of a collection of characteristic imset vectors, which are 0/1 vectors that encode the Markov equivalence class of a directed acyclic graph. These polytopes are the feasible region of linear programs which correspond to causal discovery problems. We introduce a new family of these polytopes whose vertices correspond to directed acyclic graphs with in-degree bounded by $k$. This yields a polytope whose dimension is only polynomial in the number of nodes of the underlying graphs instead of exponential. We show that when $k = 1$, this polytope is a matroid independence polytope. For $k = 2$ we provide several large families of facet-defining inequalities, which give a complete $\mathcal{H}$-representation of the polytope on four nodes.

papers.title: The enigma of locally Toeplitz matrices. I. Discrete Schr\"odinger operators with complex potential
papers.abstract: Freezing the coefficients of a banded locally Toeplitz matrix gives a family of Toeplitz eigenvalue measures. Their average can fill a region of the complex plane even when the eigenvalues of the original matrices appear to follow curves. We conjecture that, when the above average has a sufficiently regular planar density, the limiting eigenvalue measure is its mother body. We prove it for a class of finite Dirichlet discrete Schr\"odinger operators with complex potential $V$ and a common real coefficient $\alpha>0$ on the two adjacent diagonals. When $(\Im V)'>0$ and $V$ admits a suitable holomorphic extension, the limiting measure is supported on finitely many analytic arcs. Its logarithmic potential falls below that of the averaged measure by twice the least of four explicit actions. We obtain these actions from a four-term asymptotic expansion of the Dirichlet determinant. When $\Im V$ is not monotone, an exact transfer recursion gives a conditional extension. For a circular potential arc we verify the geometric switching condition, leaving non-resonance as the remaining hypothesis.

papers.title: MotionCore: A Latent Neural Simulator for Video Generation with Rigid-Body Dynamics
papers.abstract: Video generation models can produce highly realistic videos while generating physically inconsistent object motion. This limitation suggests that visual modeling alone may not provide a transferable representation of physical dynamics. We introduce MotionCore, a framework for learning physical dynamics via a learnable latent neural operator which focuses on rigid-body video generation. We introduce a latent neural simulator learning to predict the evolution of object-level physical states from observed motion. Its predictions are then converted into spatially aligned latent controls for a controllable video diffusion model. The generator serves as a visual interface: it provides appearance and scene detail, while the learned dynamics model specifies the physical trajectory. We construct our training dataset comprising semi-realistic synthetic multi-object videos with rich annotations. We evaluate MotionCore on public physical video generation benchmarks and conduct controlled ablations to assess the contribution of learned dynamics relative to other priors. Results indicate that MotionCore improves physical consistency and trajectory obedience in the evaluated rigid-body settings, while maintaining comparable visual quality. MotionCore outperforms larger general and physics-aware video generators while using substantially fewer parameters.

papers.title: JEPAhead: From Inpainting to Causal Forecasting for Urban Driving
papers.abstract: We fine-tune a pre-trained V-JEPA1 predictor from bidirectional latent inpainting to action-free causal forecasting while keeping the encoder frozen. Using contiguous past observations, horizon-aligned targets, and group-level causal attention, the model forecasts eight future token groups, corresponding to sixteen frames, in one forward pass. On CARLA Town12, it retrieves the correct future among 591 candidates in 69.0% of cases, compared with 55.3% for persistence, with greater gains at longer horizons and on tokens exhibiting greater change. It also outperforms a compact predictor trained from scratch with six times fewer parameters. Semantic analysis indicates driving-relevant information in predicted features: a fixed linear probe trained on real encoder tokens achieves 0.16 mIoU on patches undergoing semantic-class changes, versus 0.13 for persistence. Vehicle-conditioned retrieval improves over persistence by 15 percentage points at the longest horizon. Pixel-space evaluation shows modest L1 gains but little improvement under LPIPS, motivating direct evaluation through latent and semantic measures alongside an oracle reconstruction reference. These findings support further investigation of latent forecasting for driving perception, while downstream utility remains unverified.

papers.title: Same behavior, different mechanism: what finite experiments can certify about how a network computes
papers.abstract: Interpretability research, AI audits and assessments of machine consciousness make claims about how a system computes, not what it outputs. We give such claims a measurement theory. A claim is certifiable from finite interventions exactly when the mechanism lies at positive information distance from those that falsify it; it then costs at least log(1/alpha) over that distance, and an adaptive experiment attains this price asymptotically. Access, geometry and the logical form of the claim set the distance. In solvable networks, behavior carries no evidence about integrated information, and quantities that select one thing and report another have cliffs beside which cost grows as the inverse square of distance, whatever the margin. Equally accurate networks implement different circuits. In language models of up to 7.6 billion parameters, 220 of 223 audited claims about circuits, and a refusal mechanism, were certified on live interventions, 89% within the cost range registered beforehand.

papers.title: Recovery gates as a resource in repetition-code process tomography: exhaustive gate-optimal designs for three, five and seven qubits
papers.abstract: Repetition-code tomography compares a code's logical channel with a reference through a decoder, almost always standard minimum-weight. We ask how many single-qubit Pauli gates it needs with the measurement basis fixed---the constraint that makes the count a resource. Exhaustive enumeration at $n=3$, $5$ and $7$, ranks decided in exact arithmetic, gives minima of $0$, $1$ and $5$ gates, against $6$, $10$ and $14$ for first-order and $6$, $50$ and $308$ for full decoding. The count depends only on how many sites are corrected, not which, so it splits into a budget and a placement that decides identifiability; more sites is not monotonically better: at $n=7$ full decoding has rank $24$ of $27$, and the $n=3$ precision curve is U-shaped under a calibration floor. The three-gate design is $9.0$ times more precise than the standard six-gate decoder at the median of $40$ working points and better at every one, by $1.8$ to $88$-fold; fixing the placement in advance gives $6.9$, or $3.1$ for a pre-commitment never worse. Two certified placements lose no direction either sees and reach $10$\,mrad within twice the shots wherever identifiable. Measuring the reference everywhere gives a $16(n+2)$-component map, full rank at $n=3$, $5$ and $7$ with no gate and $44$ to $93\%$ fewer settings, though at $n=5$ and $7$ its floor stays one and three orders above target. The optima are not covariant under chain reversal.

papers.title: Non-Perturbative Resolution of Luttinger's Theorem Violations in Strongly Correlated Systems
papers.abstract: Many-body physics faces an apparent paradox concerning violations of Luttinger's theorem in strongly correlated systems. The theorem relates the electron number to the Luttinger count---the monodromy of the logarithm of the imaginary-frequency Green's function $\bd{G(i\epsilon)}$---and, at finite magnetic field, connects the Hall conductivity to the magnetic-field derivative of the Luttinger count via the Streda formula. Luttinger's theorem seemingly follows from particle-number conservation alone, without resorting to perturbation theory, and yet it is found to be violated. Here, we provide a non-perturbative solution to this paradox. We show that the Luttinger integral, which accounts for the mismatch between the particle number and the Luttinger count, is a pure zero-frequency boundary term, which the conventional proof implicitly discards. Hence, violations of Luttinger's theorem do not require a breakdown of the skeleton-diagram formalism, whose validity is independent of the convergence of the skeleton-diagram expansion to the exact solution. This advancement in understanding resolves a longstanding point of contention in many-body theory. We also find that the Luttinger integral is a genuine topological invariant, tied to the Luttinger-Ward functional rather than to the Green's function alone; like the monodromy of $\bd{\ln G(i\epsilon)}$, it stems exclusively from the zero-frequency point where the Matsubara trajectory crosses the branch cut of the logarithm. Correspondingly, the magnetic-field derivative of the Luttinger integral makes the Hall number in topological insulators differ from its Green's-function expression by a vertex correction, itself invariant, which can take fractional values.

papers.title: On bordism classes of symmetric products of surfaces
papers.abstract: We explicitly determine the complex bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a complex curve of genus $g$. In particular, we provide an explicit formula expressing this class as an integral linear combination of bordism classes of products of complex projective spaces. Similarly, we determine the unoriented bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a non-orientable surface of genus $g$ (i.e., $\#_{i=1}^{g+1}\mathbb R P^2$). It turns out that these classes are also expressed as a $\mathbb Z_2$-linear combination of bordism classes of products of even-dimensional real projective spaces. We also give an affirmative answer to a non-orientable version of the Blagojevi\'c--Gruji\'c--\v{Z}ivaljevi\'c conjecture stating that the topological type of any symmetric product of a noncompact surface of finite type determines the topological type of the surface itself.

papers.title: ConceptARC at Scale: Studying Conceptual Understanding in Reasoning Models
papers.abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) perform well on challenging benchmarks, yet it remains unclear whether they form generalizable abstractions across conceptually related reasoning tasks. The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) provides a controlled testbed for studying abstraction, requiring solvers to infer transformation rules over two-dimensional grids from a small set of examples. While ARC evaluates rule abstraction within individual tasks, different tasks may share higher-level structure despite requiring different transformations$\unicode{x2014}$for example, several tasks may involve reasoning about objects contained within other objects. Benchmarks such as ConceptARC capture this structure by grouping ARC-style tasks into recurring spatial and semantic concepts, but they often contain only a few manually constructed tasks per concept. We introduce ConceptARC at Scale, a generator for creating thousands of ARC-style tasks targeting a specific concept. Using this generator, we construct ConceptARC-100, a dataset of 1,600 new, manually reviewed tasks, with 100 tasks for each of the 16 concepts defined by ConceptARC$\unicode{x2014}$ten times the size of the original benchmark. We evaluate a range of recent LRMs and models trained from scratch on ConceptARC-100 to characterize which concepts they solve reliably and where they struggle. We further analyze the models' internal representations and find clear semantic structure: task representations cluster according to the operations applied to objects, such as recoloring, removal, or translation, even when realized through substantially different rules and scenarios. Together, our results suggest that models form stable abstractions of transformation operations that generalize across diverse tasks.

papers.title: Performance Analysis of EDMA-NOMA Enhanced V-SWAN-Assisted ISAC Systems
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a vertical segmented waveguide-enabled pinching antenna (V-SWAN)-assisted downlink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) environmental division multiple access (EDMA) framework for simultaneously supporting multi-user communication and target sensing. In the proposed framework, multiple pinching antennas (PAs) are deployed along a segmented vertical dielectric waveguide to serve communication users (CUs), aerial users (AUs), and sensing target (ST). CUs are distributed on the ground, whereas AUs and ST are above the ground, where line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) propagation conditions coexist. In particular, SWAN provides an effective platform for realizing EDMA by reducing the effective propagation distance and in-waveguide attenuation, thereby suppressing co-channel interference and enabling efficient multi-user transmission. The communication and sensing model are formulated, followed by the corresponding SINR expressions. We formulate the statistical characterizations for the combination of LoS and NLoS propagation for CUs, and LoS propagation for AUs and sensing channels for generalized multi-user, multi-PA scenarios. Based on these statistical characterizations, the segment outage and sensing outage probabilities are derived and evaluated for the generalized framework. The results show that the proposed framework outperforms the conventional H-SWAN and single vertical pinching antenna system (V-PASS) in terms of segment outage probability, sensing outage probability, and segment sum rate. Monte Carlo simulation results closely match the analytical results, validating the accuracy of the derived expressions. The results further highlight the impact of different system parameters on the performance of the proposed framework.

papers.title: PrimeSim: A Generalist World Model Simulator from Large-Scale Cross-Embodiment Demonstrations
papers.abstract: A robot world model that serves as a simulator must do more than generate plausible videos: it must faithfully follow commanded actions, maintain consistency across camera views, and sustain coherent long-horizon rollouts. We present PrimeSim, an action-conditioned, multiview world model simulator that addresses these challenges through progressive midtraining and posttraining. Starting from a pretrained video generator, we midtrain on 30,110 hours of robot demonstrations spanning 22 platforms. To improve action following, we introduce a unified cross-embodiment action representation and frame-aligned dual-path conditioning to strengthen action-frame correspondence. To maintain multiview consistency, we develop view-aware interleaved attention with explicit camera identities, enabling cross-view information exchange while preserving view-specific representations. We further introduce a fast-video, slow-memory posttraining framework that transforms the bidirectional video generator into an efficient autoregressive simulator. By combining fast causal generation, self-rollout training, and hierarchical temporal memory, PrimeSim mitigates error accumulation from self-generated histories and supports coherent long-horizon simulation. PrimeSim runs at 10.1 FPS, remains stable over long-horizon rollouts on rigid and deformable manipulation tasks, and transfers to held-out platforms within 100 to 200 gradient steps where the pretrained backbone does not. Against five open-source action-conditioned world models it leads four of the five WorldSimProbe suites and posts the best overall EWMBench score, while fine-grained local calibration still trails the field; its rollouts are faithful enough to support GRPO-based policy optimization. We release the model weights, inference code, and training code.

papers.title: Hidden Triakontadipole Order in the Triangular-Lattice Magnet CeMgAl$_{11}$O$_{19}$
papers.abstract: The absence of magnetic Bragg peaks and a broad excitation continuum are commonly recognized experimental features of a quantum spin liquid. The Ce-based triangular-lattice hexaaluminate CeMgAl$_{11}$O$_{19}$ exhibits both signatures, yet its effective model and ground state remain under debate. Experiments have variously suggested a quantum spin liquid, proximate umbrella point, and disorder-suppressed magnetic order. Here we trace these contradictions to an overlooked multipolar degree of freedom, and establish a dipole--triakontadipole XXZ model with $J_{\perp} \simeq 0.65$ K and $J_c \simeq -0.13$ K via precision tensor-network calculations. The resulting planar triakontadipolar superfluid order is hidden from dipolar probes, explaining the absence of a magnetic Bragg peak in neutron scattering. The zero-field excitations separate into a low-energy triakontadipole wave and a broad higher-energy continuum. We further propose nuclear spin-lattice relaxation and spin-current experiments to probe the gapless excitations of this hidden triakontadipole superfluid. Our findings thus offer a hidden-order caveat for spin-liquid searches and provide a new platform for exploring high-rank multipolar physics in rare-earth triangular-lattice magnets.

papers.title: AceAction-5M: Hierarchical Goals for Generalist Action Learning Across 3D Game Worlds
papers.abstract: Video games provide a practical setting for collecting vision-language-action (VLA) data, whose acquisition in physical environments is costly. Existing datasets, however, remain limited by restricted game coverage, sparse language supervision, or temporal hierarchies that do not necessarily reflect changes in task objectives. We introduce AceAction, a dataset of human gameplay across multiple 3D games for learning skill composition and subgoal transitions. AceAction organizes demonstrations around complete tasks, linking overall instructions, ordered subgoals, and local skill instructions to temporally aligned visual observations and keyboard-and-mouse actions. To construct these annotations, we develop a vision-language model pipeline that identifies subgoals from changes in objectives or interaction targets, anchors navigation goals to visually recognizable waypoints, and composes adjacent subgoals into task instructions. The resulting demonstrations cover navigation, reconnaissance, combat, interaction, and recovery, with explicit stage boundaries that connect task progression to fine-grained control. We assess annotation quality through model-based verification and human inspection. An audit of 500 trajectories yields a 95.8% pass rate across independent reviewer assessments. AceAction provides a data foundation for studying how agents execute, combine, and switch skills to follow complex instructions in dynamic game environments.

papers.title: Evaluating LLM Research Agents as Tests of Return Predictability
papers.abstract: How often do research agents built on large language models report that they can forecast returns when the data contain no signal? We score the conclusions of four such agents as statistical decisions on the same simulated monthly return series. Without a prescribed significance level, the agents reported that their forecasts would beat the expanding historical mean in 16-44% of 110 null samples, whereas a Holm-adjusted regression test rejected the absence of predictability in 8% of the same samples. When a weak predictor was present, comparisons at matched false-positive rates did not establish a detection advantage for the three commercial agents. Instructing those agents to report outperformance only if they would reject the absence of predictability at the 5% level, accounting for every specification they evaluated, reduced their false-positive rates to 0-3%. It also reduced detection at a population $R^2$ of 1%: from 74% to 45% for Claude Opus 5.5, from 59% to 6% for GPT-6.1 Sol and from 71% to 15% for GPT-6.1 Terra. Whether the instruction holds the false-positive rate at 5% remains unresolved. For researchers who delegate the search for return predictors to an agent, specifying the final comparison deserves as much attention as choosing the forecasting model.

papers.title: Beyond the Federer paradox in tennis
papers.abstract: Roger Federer won about 80% of his professional matches with only 54% of the points. Hierarchical scoring amplifies small advantages on points into large advantages on matches, but also allows a player to win with fewer points than the opponent. Using Monte Carlo simulations and exact Markov chain calculations, we show that in tennis, badminton, volleyball and table tennis this amplification is set almost entirely by the number of points per match. We then let a player win ordinary points with probability p1 and crucial points, those closing a game, set or match, with probability p2. In every sport a narrow region of the (p1, p2) plane exists where a player wins most matches with fewer than half of the points, because crucial points carry more influence than their share of points. Of ATP matches played in 1991-2025, 4.7% were won with fewer points, 16% more than independent points predict (5% including the serve), a constant excess. Pressure performance measured in other seasons predicts match outcomes beyond the points won, and Fabio Fognini won 51% of his matches with 49% of the points, in what we call the Fognini paradox.

papers.title: Uniform Sampling of Linear Codes with Prescribed Hull Dimension
papers.abstract: We give exactly uniform samplers for linear codes with prescribed hull dimension, for the Euclidean, Hermitian, and symplectic inner products and over finite fields of every characteristic. Except for the Euclidean form over fields of odd characteristic, these are the first uniform samplers for arbitrary prescribed hull dimension. Each sample costs an expected $O(k^2 N + k \log q)$ field operations for codes of dimension $k$ in a space of dimension $N$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ or $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$.

papers.title: Generalizable Equivariant Diffusion Models for Non-Abelian Lattice Gauge Theory: Analytical Foundations and Numerical Scaling Tests
papers.abstract: Gauge-equivariant diffusion models can be used to generate ensembles of field configurations in non-abelian lattice gauge theories. Previously, we demonstrated the feasibility of modeling these theories by combining L-CNN-based diffusion models with the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA). Here we focus on the underlying analytical framework. In particular, we present a rigorous derivation of the reverse-time stochastic differential equation on the group manifold, discuss the gauge invariance of the denoising loss function, and provide extensive numerical benchmarks regarding the scaling behavior with respect to the lattice volume and the inverse coupling $\beta$. Full analytical expressions for arbitrarily sized Wilson loops and the topological charge susceptibility during the forward process are given as well.

papers.title: The proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: a detailed exposition and an extension to rotation systems
papers.abstract: The Harary--Hill conjecture states that the crossing number $\ucr{K_n}$ of the complete graph $K_n$ is $Z(n):=\frac{1}{4}\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\rfloor$ for all $n\ge 3$. In October 2026 OpenAI uploaded to GitHub a proof of this conjecture. The proof is very short, but it relies on polynomial methods that are not part of the standard techniques used by many combinatorialists, and it is written with very little motivation or explanation. Since we found the proof very hard to follow, we decided to write this paper, which contains a complete proof of the conjecture written for mathematicians who are more familiar with combinatorics than with polynomial methods. In fact we prove a more general result on rotation systems of $K_n$, from which the Harary--Hill conjecture easily follows. Namely, we show that for every rotation system $\Pi$ of $K_n$ the number of $4$-vertex subsystems of $\Pi$ realizable as drawings of $K_4$ with one crossing, plus three times the number of non-realizable $4$-vertex subsystems of $\Pi$, is at least $Z(n)$. The statement and proof of our result are purely combinatorial and do not involve drawings at all.

papers.title: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
papers.abstract: We construct a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton. The instanton has Euler characteristic $\chi = 4$ and Hirzebruch signature $\tau = -1$. The topology at infinity is a lens space $L(3,1)$. The solution depends on one parameter and is constructed from the Belinski--Zakharov four-soliton solution. We prove that the instanton is smooth and positive definite on and away from the axis. This is the first example of a non-Hermitian ALF (not AF) gravitational instanton.

papers.title: Can You Predict the Next Mind in the Symphony? Toward Multi-Turn Multi-Party Mental World Modeling
papers.abstract: Although multimodal foundation models have achieved remarkable progress in modeling, generation, and embodied reasoning in the physical world, their capacity for modeling the dynamic mental world remains underexplored. Existing benchmarks predominantly focus on static mental state perception or single-turn behavioral reasoning, overlooking the dynamic mental transitions of the observed individuals in multi-party, multi-turn interactions. To bridge this gap, we introduce M$^3$WME-Bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate mental world modeling conditioned on evolving actions of interactants. Specifically, models are tasked with forecasting a target subject's future mental states and behaviors over extended social interactions. In addition to the benchmark suite, we construct M$^3$WME-23K, a dedicated training dataset, and establish a competitive baseline named MindNext-7B. Extensive evaluations across four representative paradigms (general MLLMs, emotion-specialized MLLMs, agentic frameworks, and World Foundation Models) reveal that current systems consistently struggle to anticipate forward-looking mental states. Mechanistic analyses further reveal that existing architectures fundamentally lack forward mental state transition dynamics. Our findings highlight a pivotal challenge in advancing agents from physical to mental world modeling, charting new directions for socially adaptive AI.

papers.title: Solv3R: 3D Looped Transformer as a Multi-view Solver
papers.abstract: Classical structure-from-motion reconstruction proceeds iteratively, refining camera poses and scene geometry from a current estimate. This allows maps to easily expand without recomputing solved views, or geometry estimates to improve as more observations are provided. Most geometric foundation models, however, predict entire geometry in a single forward pass or update a recurrent state as frames arrive sequentially, making this expansion and refinement non-trivial. We introduce Solv3R, a looped transformer that learns to continue solving multi-view geometry from its current state. Importantly, its update operator is independent of the iteration count, allowing previously refined and newly introduced views to be updated jointly or selectively, regardless of how ``solved'' they are. We train the operator to preserve accurate reconstructions under continued iteration and correct inaccurate states, enabling refinement of fixed image collections and integration of new observations. Representations of solved views can also be cached once and reused as geometric context across iterations, enabling compact and efficient key-value caching. We analyze the solver dynamics and compare it with the state-of-the-art, showing that a single learned solver supports offline and incremental reconstruction, relocalization, and streaming without task-specific training or learned modules. The code and model are available at https://github.com/ubc-vision/solv3r.

papers.title: Targeting the future of spectroscopic galaxy surveys -- A cosmological study case with the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope
papers.abstract: The next generation of Stage-V spectroscopic surveys are designed to measure hundreds of millions of galaxy and quasar spectra, extending precision large-scale-structure cosmology to redshifts and volumes well beyond the reach of current Stage-IV facilities. Realising this potential requires revisiting the target selection strategies and designing them explicitly around the depth, multiplexing, and survey time of the new instruments, rather than a direct extrapolation of existing recipes. This work develops and characterises new strategies for the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST), a proposed 12-metre, highly multiplexed facility expected to operate in the 2040s. Using deep multi-band photometry, including COSMOS-field data from CLAUDS and HSC, we revisit low-redshift $z \lesssim 1.6$ tracer selection of SDSS, BOSS/eBOSS, DESI and 4MOST-CRS -- Bright Galaxies, Luminous Red Galaxies, Emission Line Galaxies and quasars -- to photometric depth achievable in the WST era, and introduce a purely magnitude-limited sample (MagMax) exploiting three-dimensional color-color star-galaxy separation, and a set of Lyman-Break Galaxy dropout samples extending target selection to $z \gtrsim 2$.
